name: Gear & Retail
chart_note: Specialty running and outdoor retailers, gear brands and mass-market stores. Bubble = US monthly search volume (area-scaled and capped so Walmart at 68M and Nike at 24.9M do not swamp the 246k specialty rows); grey band = the middle half of the entities on this chart (-0.019 to +0.030).
insight_title:
ROAD RUNNER SPORTS AND REI,
NOT WALMART
insight:
Road Runner Sports is the top retailer in the category at +0.072, with REI second at +0.043 - the specialty running and outdoor channel, on the left of the political axis. Hydro Flask and the Nike Outlet store-locator search sit at the upper edge of the band, and Scheels just inside it; Scheels is the one over-indexer that leans right, which is the Upper Midwest and mountain geography showing through rather than a politics.

The mass-discount channel is the mirror image. Walmart is the weakest entity at -0.059 and Academy Sports is below the band at -0.021; both sit on the right of the political axis. Nike itself, at 24.9 million searches a month, is neutral (-0.014): the bare brand is a mass word, and the outlet-shopping intent sits above it. Among gear brands Hydro Flask (+0.030) and Yeti (-0.037) split on the segment axis, though on this chart both lean slightly left, so the split is a purchase-culture split rather than a political one.

One honest correction: Fleet Feet, the largest specialty running franchise in the country, sits inside the band at -0.011. The specialty-retail story is real, but it runs through Road Runner Sports and REI, not through Fleet Feet - co-op, in-store and partnership inventory should follow those two, with Scheels as the regional add.
